chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Hearing Fletcher Henderson's band in Cincinnati in 1930
summary: Jackson calls it the most fantastic band he had heard and lists its trumpets, trombones, saxophones and rhythm section with Kirby, Walter Johnson and Clarence Holiday.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I remember way back when -- well, the first time I heard that band that I thought it was the most fantastic band I had ever heard and that was in 1930. I heard them in Cincinnati, Ohio.
That was Fletcher Henderson's band?
That's right.
Who was in the -- ?
The trumpets at that time was Russell Pop Pot Smith and Rex Stewart and Bobby Stark
Wow. Bobby Stark.
Yeah, and the trombones was Jimmy Harrison and Claude Jones.
Wow.
Saxophones was Bennie Carter, Harvey Boone, and Coleman Hawkins.
Harvey Boone?

Yeah. Good saxophone player. He could play oboe, flute, piccolo. He was a guy that was jack of all trades. He was a good barber. He made all his saxophone stands himself. He was that type of guy. Not much of a soloist but could play, if you put the music there, he would play it.
Oh.
And the bass player then was John Kirby. He was nothing but a kid at the time. And the guitar player was Clarence Holliday, which is Billie Holliday's father.
Wow.
The great Billie Holliday, it was her father.
Uh-huh.

And Walter Johnson was on drums which to me is one of the smoothest drummers that ever lived. Here's a guy that could play a gig all night, I don't care how hot the weather was, and at the end of the dance his shirt looked just like he just put it on.
That's right, I always heard that.
Never, his shirt never wilted or nothing. He was as sharp as he could be. A very neat gentleman and a quiet gentleman. I admire Walter so much. And that was the band.
Uh-huh.
That was one of the greatest rhythm sections that I ever heard. It was when with Holliday or Fletcher and --
Fletcher and John Kirby.

-- John Kirby, sure, and Walter Johnson. Oh, my goodness. I heard them out to -- they played a party out to Walnut Hill for some rich people and I went out there that night to hear the band. I was astounded because I'd never heard nothing like that.
